claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital for 12 weeks (within 12-week limit)
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old are the children you're claiming for?** 

To help me guide you through the eligibility assessment, I need to know:

1. **What is/are the age(s) of your child/children?** (Please provide the age of each child you're inquiring about)

The age categories are:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **16 to 19 years old** 
- **20 years old or over**

Once I know their ages, I can help determine which children might qualify and guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're claiming for **Alex, who is 8 years old** and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is under 16, he falls into the qualifying age category. Now I need to check a few more things to determine your eligibility. Let me proceed with the next question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 8 years old, he's unlikely to be in paid work, but I need to confirm this for the assessment. Please let me know:
- Is he in any paid employment? 
- If yes, how many hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all. He's only 8, so he's just at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear - Alex is not working and is at school, which is perfect. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right?**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

Please let me know if Alex receives either of these benefits. Since he's 8, it's unlikely he would be, but I need to confirm for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's 8 years old and at school, this is almost certainly "no," but I need to ask for completeness: Is Alex currently in any kind of apprenticeship programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not. He's only 8 - he's in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely! That makes sense - Alex is clearly not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important part of the eligibility criteria.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

To help me understand your situation better, please tell me:
- Where do you and Alex normally live?
- Are you a UK resident, or do you have a different residency status?

There are several residency paths that can qualify you, including:
- Normally living in the UK
- Having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Certain circumstances for pre-settled status (working, studying, jobseeking, or with sufficient resources)
- Being a Crown servant living abroad in qualifying countries

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. We live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK in Manchester. That satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means one of the following:
- You live with him (which you've already told me you do)
- You contribute to his upkeep (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.)
- You pay maintenance towards his care under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned Alex lives at home with you, you're clearly responsible for him. Can you confirm this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me and I take care of him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you live with Alex and you're responsible for his care. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied for it?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent also claiming for him?
- Has anyone else applied or told you they might claim for him?

Please let me know if there are any other claimants involved or if it's just you claiming for Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming for him. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So you're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Where is Alex currently living?**

I need to check if any special circumstances apply:
- Is he in hospital?
- Is he in care (local authority care)?
- Is he being fostered?
- Or is he living normally at home with you in Manchester?

What's his current living situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for a while now, actually. About three months.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I see - Alex has been in hospital for about three months. Let me check the specific rules around hospital stays.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I need to get some more details about Alex's hospital stay to apply the rules correctly.

**A few important questions about Alex's hospital stay:**

1. **Has this been one continuous stay of 3 months, or has he had multiple hospital stays?**
   - If multiple stays, when did each one start and end?

2. **If there have been gaps between stays, how long were those gaps?** (This matters because there's a special "linking rule" - if he returns to hospital within 28 days of leaving, the time counts together)

3. **Before this current hospital stay, had Alex been in hospital in the previous 28 days?**

The reason I ask is that Child Benefit can continue for up to 12 weeks (cumulative) in hospital. If the total time exceeds 12 weeks, there are different rules that apply. Let me know the details so I can check your eligibility correctly.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been one continuous stay - he's been there for the full three months without coming home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. So Alex has been in hospital continuously for 3 months (approximately 12 weeks). Let me check the next part of the rules.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in the hospital?**

This is important because there's an exception to the 12-week rule. If you're regularly spending money on Alex (beyond what the hospital provides), you may still be eligible. 

Examples of regular spending could include:
- Buying him clothes, toiletries, or personal items
- Paying for entertainment or comfort items
- Contributing to his care costs
- Travel expenses to visit him

Are you regularly spending your own money on Alex while he's in hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I still buy his clothes, magazines, and his favorite food to bring to him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good - you're regularly spending money on Alex's care and comfort while he's in the hospital. That's an important factor. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance in the hospital?**

In other words:
- Is the local council (Manchester City Council in your case) paying for his hospital stay or contributing to his care costs?
- Or are you responsible for his costs while he's in hospital?

Please let me know if the council is involved in paying for his hospital care.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything. It's just the NHS hospital care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! The council is not paying - it's just NHS hospital care. Based on all the information you've provided, I now have everything I need to determine your eligibility. Let me provide you with the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

**Child:** Alex (age 8)

**Result:** ELIGIBLE

### Key Reasons:

1. ✅ **Age:** Alex is 8 years old - a qualifying age (under 16)
2. ✅ **Work status:** He's not working (he's in school)
3. ✅ **Benefits:** He's not receiving ESA or Universal Credit
4. ✅ **Apprenticeship:** He's not in any disqualifying apprenticeship
5. ✅ **Residency:** You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
6. ✅ **Responsibility:** You live with Alex and are responsible for his care
7. ✅ **No other claimant:** You're the only person claiming for him
8. ✅ **Hospital stay exception:** Although Alex has been in hospital for 3 months, you are regularly spending money on his care (clothes, magazines, food), which qualifies as an exception to the 12-week hospital limit
9. ✅ **Council not paying:** The local council is not paying for his care - it's NHS hospital care

### Next Steps:

- You can now apply for Child Benefit through the official government website: **www.gov.uk/child-benefit**
- You'll need to provide evidence of your identity, Alex's date of birth, National Insurance number, and details of your bank account
- If you have any questions during the application process, contact the Child Benefit helpline

I hope Alex makes a good recovery! Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old (under 16, a qualifying age). He is not working more than 24 hours per week. He does not receive ESA or Universal Credit in his own right. You are the only claimant for Alex. Although Alex has been in hospital for approximately 3 months (around 12 weeks, at the limit of the 12-week rule), you are regularly spending money on him while he is in hospital (buying clothes, magazines, and food), which is an exception to the standard 12-week limit. The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance - it is NHS hospital care only. All eligibility criteria are met.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Although he has been in hospital for 3 months, the fact that you are regularly spending money on his care and comfort while in hospital means the standard 12-week limit does not apply to prevent your claim. You meet all other eligibility requirements: you live in the UK, you are responsible for Alex, you are the only claimant, and the council is not paying for his care."

criteria.calculation_method: Sum all hospital/residential stays. If gap between stays is less than 28 days, count both stays towards cumulative total. If gap is 28+ days, reset counter.
